subject: TTFT & Streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: TTFT & streaming SLOs + next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex — great context on the user experience goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear qualification path: 

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: 150–200ms for typical short responses (~50–150 tokens)
- Streaming: required (end-user needs progressive token display); preference noted for WebSocket but SSE is acceptable
- Chunk cadence: target ~100–200ms between token chunks (responsiveness for UI)
- Concurrency & throughput: baseline 30 concurrent sessions, burst to 100; expected steady state ~400 requests/minute (~6.7 req/s) but some large scale-up bursts during promos
- SLOs: 95th percentile TTFT <= 200ms; p50/p90 latency targets for end-to-end streaming are helpful for pass/fail in qualification

Proposed next steps (what we'll do on our side):
1) Lauren/Rishi to run a 1–2 hour qualification/benchmark using a representative prompt set you provide. We'll test both WebSocket and SSE modes (if SSE is ok for you) and measure token cadence and TTFT.
2) We'll share a lightweight test plan and a sample payload set (attached: TTFT_Test_Plan.pdf).
3) Please confirm:
   - Which streaming protocol you'd prefer we prioritize (WebSocket or SSE)?
   - Typical response lengths (tokens) we should use for baseline and burst tests
   - Any networking constraints (corporate proxies, MTU limits) we should be aware of

I attached a short note with chunk-cadence options (streaming_cadence_notes.pdf). If that looks good I'll loop in Rishi (infrastructure) to schedule the run and we can book a 1-hour window next week.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0112
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TTFT & streaming SLOs + next steps

Thanks Marissa — this matches our notes and the team is aligned. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT: we can accept up to 200ms at p95 for short responses (<=100 tokens). For longer responses (200–400 tokens) p95 can be higher but user experience should still show incremental tokens quickly.
- Streaming protocol: our frontend team prefers WebSocket (bidirectional) because we may send intermediate user edits; SSE is acceptable if latency is demonstrably better, but our preference is WebSocket.
- Chunk cadence: 120–180ms is ideal for perceived responsiveness; anything above ~250ms starts to feel laggy to our UX team.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline 30 concurrent streaming connections per region; we need to handle bursts up to ~100 concurrent connections for peak events. For request/second numbers, aim for being able to sustain 100 req/s in a single region during peak testing with headroom.

I'll attach our internal perf matrix (acme_perf_matrix.csv) so you have expected payload sizes and a few sample prompts. We'll also share a small sample dataset (3–5 prompts) by EOD tomorrow that you can use for the baseline runs.

Last ask: from procurement — if the qualification looks good we may need a short formal report (latency breakdown p50/p90/p95, token cadence distribution, and recommended config) to attach to our vendor review packet. Can you confirm Redwood can provide that?

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Johnson
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acme-retail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TTFT & streaming SLOs + next steps

Perfect, thanks for the clarifications and the perf matrix, Alex. We can absolutely produce a short qualification report that includes p50/p90/p95 TTFT, token cadence histograms, and configuration recommendations for production (batching, quantization profile, routing policy).

Operational plan & next steps from Redwood: 
- Qualification window: Proposed Wed Mar 18, 02:00–04:00 PT (we'll provision a dedicated cluster for the run so results aren't noisy). Please confirm if that works for your team.
- Protocols: We'll test both WebSocket-first and SSE fallback. Since you prefer WebSocket we'll run that scenario first.
- Test artifacts: We'll use your sample prompts (please drop them in the Drive link) and our standard payload variants (short/medium/long). We'll capture per-token timings, network RTT, and model compute time for TTFT breakdown.
- Deliverables: After the run we'll provide: 1) one-page executive summary (pass/fail vs your SLOs), 2) detailed metrics (p50/p90/p95), 3) raw logs and script to reproduce, 4) recommended config and cost estimate for Dedicated capacity if you want a dedicated pool for production.

Action items for you (Alex):
- Share the sample prompts and confirm Wed window or propose an alternative.
- If you have an IP allowlist or proxy details we need to use for the test, share those now so we can configure the demo infra.

I'll attach the TTFT_Test_Plan.pdf and streaming_cadence_notes.pdf again for reference. Looping in Rishi + Lauren to schedule the infra and own the run.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Quick confirmation from infra: Wed 2026-03-18 02:00–04:00 PT works (we'll spin up a dedicated small cluster with the quantized model variant and instrument token-level latency). We'll produce the metrics you requested and upload results + raw traces to the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/ttft/TTFT-Test-Run-8741.

- Run 3 phases: ramp (30 concurrent), steady (30), burst (100) — each 20 minutes.
- Output: p50/p90/p95 TTFT, token cadence distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, and a short config recommendation.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the runbook.
